content: 1. It is essential to eliminate any discriminatory language and reinforce the principles of respect and human rights in all leprosy-related training programs for healthcare workers. 2. Ensure the availability and use of contextualized information, education, and communication (IEC) materials to provide accurate information and address specific fears and beliefs related to leprosy. 3. Incorporate at least one additional stigma reduction strategy, such as direct contact with individuals affected by leprosy, in all leprosy program plans, beyond merely providing information. 4. Include interventions aimed at promoting empowerment and providing psychosocial support to individuals affected by leprosy in all program plans. 5. Consider involving religious leaders to help reduce stigma and discrimination within communities. 6. Individuals affected by leprosy should play a significant role in leprosy services, particularly in advocacy, awareness generation, and fostering inclusion. 7. Organized efforts by individuals affected by leprosy are necessary to promote a positive perception of the disease, advocate for changes in discriminatory legal measures, policies, and practices, and ensure leprosy remains a priority in national health policy frameworks. 8. There is a lack of awareness among policymakers and health managers about the importance of involving individuals for whom services are designed in planning and evaluation processes. 9. The contributions of individuals who have experienced leprosy to their communities are often insufficiently recognized. 10. Ensuring that individuals affected by leprosy are central to program planning, delivery, and evaluation will significantly impact the quality and effectiveness of services. 11. These guidelines emphasize the expertise of individuals who have experienced leprosy and encourage partnerships to enable their active participation in service delivery. 12. Efforts should be made to create opportunities for individuals to engage in leprosy services, ultimately leading to equal access to quality services and respect for their roles as contributing members of society. 13. Practical examples of how affected individuals can participate in health, social, and other services should be demonstrated and structurally embedded. 14. Promising initiatives should be developed into demonstration models through operational research to guide future policies and practices. 15. The Stigma Assessment and Reduction of Impact Project in Indonesia demonstrated the effectiveness of various interventions, including counseling, empowerment, socioeconomic development, and community contact, in reducing leprosy-related stigma. 16. Contact interventions, such as testimonies, participatory videos, and comics created by individuals affected by leprosy, facilitated dialogue between affected individuals and community members, significantly improving knowledge and attitudes about leprosy. 17. Community members should be actively involved in disseminating health education, referring suspected cases, organizing health camps, promoting treatment adherence, and supporting individuals with disabilities in self-care management. 18. Specific subgroups within communities, such as family members, health volunteers, traditional healers, and religious leaders, should be engaged to address their fears, attitudes, and beliefs about leprosy and mobilize them to reduce stigma and improve services. 19. Positive examples of female health volunteers in India, Indonesia, and Nepal highlight their critical role in case detection and community support. 20. Associations like the Ethiopia National Association of People Affected by Leprosy (ENAPAL) advocate for the rights of individuals affected by leprosy, raise awareness, and promote socioeconomic empowerment, transforming lives from begging to dignified livelihoods. 21. ENAPAL operates in multiple regions, mobilizing NGOs and community-based organizations to address the needs of its members and advocate for leprosy-related issues. 22. At the global and regional levels, training materials should be developed to implement guidelines on involving individuals affected by leprosy in service delivery. 23. Operational research should be conducted to build models demonstrating how affected individuals' participation can be structurally embedded in various contexts. 24. Sharing experiences between countries and programs, as well as within the scientific and public health communities, should be encouraged to improve the involvement of leprosy-affected individuals in services. 25. National policies should include the participation of individuals affected by leprosy in service delivery and promote their empowerment to advocate for legislative and policy changes. 26. Community-based organizations (CBOs) should be supported through partnerships to sustain community support groups and improve access to services. 27. Training should be provided to community partners to facilitate access and improve leprosy services. 28. Advocacy and negotiations are needed to expand social protection coverage for individuals affected by leprosy, addressing their unique needs and economic burdens. 29. International organizations like IDEA advocate for the rights of individuals affected by leprosy, emphasizing their right to full and equal participation in society without discrimination. 30. Peer groups and self-help organizations provide moral, psychological, social, and practical support, helping individuals affected by leprosy to practice effective self-care and prevent further disabilities. 31. Self-help groups often evolve into socioeconomic development initiatives, empowering members to advocate for their rights and improve services collectively. 32. Governments and NGOs should collaborate with organized groups of affected individuals, inviting their representatives to participate in consultations and decision-making processes. 33. Membership in self-help groups has been shown to reduce internalized stigma, improve self-esteem, and combat depression among individuals affected by leprosy. 34. Training in organizational skills, governance, human rights, and advocacy techniques should be provided to leaders and representatives of affected individuals' organizations. 35. Partnerships with NGOs and other organizations can facilitate empowerment and provide opportunities for affected individuals to gain experience in governance and advocacy. 36. National leprosy programs and NGOs should formalize the roles of affected individuals' organizations through memoranda of understanding to ensure their involvement in service delivery and advocacy. 37. Continued advocacy is necessary to improve access to social and financial support services for individuals affected by leprosy, addressing the economic burdens and social challenges they face.
